name: Denise Emery
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember putting on street clothes without feeling ready to leave.” Friday often includes a stop at the window at Night Shift Donuts, where Denise knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I ticked footwear present on the form. I have added a chair where people can actually try the pair.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a plum-colored cardigan and a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip. Denise has a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, with a high puff tied with plain cord. Denise looks toward the door whenever a name is called during a conversation.
personality: Denise tells a better story in a kitchen than at a microphone. Family members sometimes underestimate how far Denise will go to back a quiet opinion once it is actually challenged.
agenda: To give discharged patients a real chance to try their shoes.
family: Carla Lam is Denise’s cousin. Denise gets to change the plan. Carla offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The dead man's tab*, Carla says, “I was his lawyer. He never once asked me to wipe out this particular debt.”
connections: Lena Sanders. They design a discharge fitting with a seat and some privacy. Also in the story is Irene Franco (hospital colleague).

reactions.situation: A patient opens the bag and finds two left slippers
reactions.response: Denise sets out the pair and asks the discharge worker to check the right foot too.

reactions.situation: Somebody finds a lost wallet outside the bank
reactions.response: Denise keeps the documents out of view and lets the person claiming it identify it before hearing any details.

reactions.situation: If a relative makes a joke at a child's expense
reactions.response: Denise repeats the child's actual point and waits for a reply to that.
